dossier.public_summary: The 0.56-day dip is locked exactly to the star's own 0.561-day spot cycle and varies in depth from sector to sector, with an out-of-eclipse brightness swing almost as large as the dip itself. Together this shows the signal is stellar spin/pulsation, not a planet transit. The on-target location rules out a background eclipsing binary, but the variability pattern matches a highly spotted short-period M dwarf folding with its rotation.

reasons.why: A sinusoidal out-of-eclipse swing of the same amplitude as the 12400 ppm dip (ratio 1.078) is stellar in shape: a hot Jupiter/ob EBB would not show this on a 0.3758 R_sun M dwarf. The depth and luminosity are locked, pointing to spots/variability folded at orbital period.

The 0.561 d signal is exactly the star's spot period in every sector, not a period close to it by chance. This phase-alignment plus the amplitude comparable to the dip shows the dip is not a transit, but modulation from a highly spotted / short-rotation M dwarf.
reasons.value: signal_over_rotation 1.0001978609625668 rotation_d 0.561 signal_period_d 0.561111 amplitude_ppm 15156 to 37245 false_alarm 0.0 to 1.6e-42

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor ~3.7 (111% change, chi2 127.4 dof 3) even within TESS-SPOC, inconsistent with a geometric transit. Depth tracks spot coverage/aperture, as expected when the 'dip' is part of the rotation signal.

reasons.why: Duration (1.247 h vs 0.7927 h central) and stellar density imply a log density ratio -1.678 with penalty 2096, inconsistent with a planet around a 0.3758 R_sun star. With larger Gaia radii (FLAME 0.456 R, GSP-Phot 0.459 R) ratios become 1.29/1.28 but the phase-lock remains; the inconsistency positively favours intrinsic variability, including a grazing/contact variable.

reasons.why: Argument for an off-target blended EB is excluded: centroid difference imaging puts the dip on the target (2.145 sigma) and rules out neighbours needing eclipses (30.6 arcsec suspect 32.2 sigma away). The signal is on-target but stellar, so an EB on the target is the closest binary interpretation still rejected by phase curve + depth change, leaving stellar variability as best.
